29ac91659d9b.zh: 這一章在講什麼：一張從生物到深度學習的地圖
29ac91659d9b.en: What this chapter is about: a map from biology to deep learning

2b76f0348db1.zh: 人工神經網路是現代機器學習裡最有力量的工具之一，舉凡電腦視覺、自然語言處理，背後都靠它。而這些看似複雜的系統，核心其實是一個很簡單的運算單元——受到生物神經元啟發的「人工神經元」。要搞懂深度學習，就得先搞懂這個基礎積木，以及它如何一步步演化過來。這一章就是這張地圖。
2b76f0348db1.en: Artificial neural networks are among the most powerful tools in modern machine learning; computer vision and natural language processing alike rely on them. And at the core of these seemingly complex systems is actually a very simple computational unit: the "artificial neuron", inspired by the biological neuron. To understand deep learning, you first have to understand this basic building block and how it evolved step by step. This chapter is that map.

66bdf61f5981.zh: 全章的敘事是一條清楚的四段結構，跟著走就不會迷路：
66bdf61f5981.en: The chapter's narrative follows a clear four-part structure; follow it and you won't get lost:

772658d5c0cb.zh: 從 Perceptron 出發（§2）：Perceptron 是神經網路史上最早、也最有影響力的模型之一。它雖然簡單，卻帶出了幾個貫穿全書的關鍵概念——加權輸入、激活函數、以及根據回饋（錯誤）更新權重的學習規則。
772658d5c0cb.en: Starting from the perceptron (§2): the perceptron is one of the earliest and most influential models in the history of neural networks. Simple as it is, it introduces several key concepts that run through the whole book: weighted inputs, activation functions, and a learning rule that updates the weights based on feedback (errors).

25b6a276f0d9.zh: 推進到 MLP（§2 後段）：Perceptron 有個致命傷——它無法解像 XOR 這類非線性分類問題。這個限制推動了更具表達力的模型誕生，也就是 Multi-Layer Perceptron（MLP）／前饋神經網路，它能把輸入疊成多層，畫出更複雜的決策邊界。
25b6a276f0d9.en: Moving on to the MLP (later in §2): the perceptron has a fatal weakness: it cannot solve non-linear classification problems such as XOR. This limitation drove the birth of more expressive models, namely the multi-layer perceptron (MLP) / feedforward neural network, which stacks the input into multiple layers and can draw more complex decision boundaries.

1619f1b1e428.zh: 補充模型（旁支）（§3）：ADALINE、logistic regression、RBF 網路、SOM 等模型，不是主線，但提供寶貴的歷史與概念脈絡，幫你把神經網路放進更廣的早期機器學習光譜裡。
1619f1b1e428.en: Supplementary models (side branches) (§3): models such as ADALINE, logistic regression, RBF networks and SOM are not the main line, but they provide valuable historical and conceptual context, helping you place neural networks within the broader spectrum of early machine learning.

041e1626bc70.zh: UAT 收尾（§4）：Universal Approximation Theorem（萬有逼近定理）保證：只要有足夠的神經元，神經網路就能把一大類函數逼近到任意精度——這就是「表達能力」的理論保證。
041e1626bc70.en: Wrapping up with the UAT (§4): the universal approximation theorem guarantees that, given enough neurons, a neural network can approximate a broad class of functions to arbitrary precision. This is the theoretical guarantee of "expressive power".

059e03817a8f.zh: 為什麼一定要先學 Perceptron
059e03817a8f.en: Why you have to learn the perceptron first

d3ec293fc4ae.zh: 你可能會想：都 2020 年代了，還學一個 1958 年的老古董幹嘛？因為 Perceptron 把深度學習的「三根支柱」一次示範得清清楚楚：
d3ec293fc4ae.en: You might be thinking: it's the 2020s, why bother learning an antique from 1958? Because the perceptron demonstrates the "three pillars" of deep learning crystal clearly, all at once:

eff7fcad6744.zh: 加權輸入（weighted inputs）：每個輸入乘上一個權重再相加，權重大小代表這個輸入有多重要。
eff7fcad6744.en: Weighted inputs: each input is multiplied by a weight and then they are summed; the size of a weight represents how important that input is.

e648edda301f.zh: 激活函數（activation function）：對加權和做一個「開關」式的轉換，決定神經元要不要「發火」。
e648edda301f.en: Activation function: applies a "switch"-like transformation to the weighted sum, deciding whether the neuron "fires".

cf938bba1385.zh: 權重更新（weight update）：根據預測錯誤，回饋式地調整權重——這就是「學習」的雛形。
cf938bba1385.en: Weight update: adjusts the weights based on prediction errors, as feedback. This is the embryonic form of "learning".

2e3314765cc5.zh: 只要掌握了這三件事，後面 MLP 的所有內容，不過是把這個單元「疊很多層」、再把激活函數換成更平滑的非線性函數而已。
2e3314765cc5.en: Once you've mastered these three things, everything that follows about the MLP is nothing more than "stacking many layers" of this unit and swapping the activation function for a smoother non-linear function.

6799c2e17fc3.zh: 一張伏筆：XOR 為什麼是轉捩點
6799c2e17fc3.en: A bit of foreshadowing: why XOR is the turning point

7fd87485dce3.zh: 本章最常被拿出來講的例子是 XOR：當兩類資料沒辦法用「一條直線」切開時，單一 Perceptron 就無能為力。這個「非線性可分」的缺口，正是引出多層架構的最大伏筆——留著，後面 kp6 會回頭細講，而 MLP 之所以存在，很大一部分就是為了補上這個洞。
7fd87485dce3.en: The example most often brought up in this chapter is XOR: when two classes of data cannot be separated by "one straight line", a single perceptron is helpless. This "not linearly separable" gap is exactly the biggest piece of foreshadowing that leads to multi-layer architectures. Hold on to it; kp6 will come back to it in detail, and the MLP exists in large part precisely to fill this hole.

a7c215315a90.en: The four-part journey: Perceptron → MLP → Supplementary models → UAT

e48bcfe910d1.zh: 從一顆活的神經細胞講起
e48bcfe910d1.en: Starting from a Living Nerve Cell

4542f1619ec4.zh: 人工神經網路是由「人工神經元」組成的，而這個名字不是隨便取的——它鬆散地受到生物神經元的啟發（loosely inspired）。所以理解真正的生物神經元怎麼運作，能讓我們看懂人工版本在模仿什麼。圖（Fig. 1）畫出了一顆生物神經元的主要構造。
4542f1619ec4.en: Artificial neural networks are made of "artificial neurons," and the name wasn't picked at random: they are loosely inspired by biological neurons. So understanding how a real biological neuron works helps us see what the artificial version is imitating. The figure (Fig. 1) shows the main structure of a biological neuron.

e0b07691586e.zh: 一顆生物神經元有幾個關鍵部件，各司其職：
e0b07691586e.en: A biological neuron has a few key parts, each with its own job:

4bc9e40fb8b2.zh: Soma（細胞體）：神經元的「本體」，負責把收到的訊號整合起來——可以想成一座城的市中心，所有訊息最後都匯到這裡。
4bc9e40fb8b2.en: Soma (cell body): the "main body" of the neuron, responsible for integrating the signals it receives. Think of it as a city's downtown, where all messages eventually converge.

e5689ded28c2.zh: Nucleus（細胞核）：位於 Soma 內部，存放遺傳物質、調控細胞活動——是細胞的「指揮中心」。
e5689ded28c2.en: Nucleus: located inside the soma, it stores the genetic material and regulates the cell's activity. It is the cell's "command center."

8fffee45031d.zh: Dendrites（樹突）：像樹枝一樣的延伸結構，負責接收來自其他神經元的電化學訊號，並把訊號往 Soma 方向傳送——是神經元的「天線」。
8fffee45031d.en: Dendrites: branch-like extensions responsible for receiving electrochemical signals from other neurons and passing them toward the soma. They are the neuron's "antennas."

ed487e0894c7.zh: Synapse（突觸）：一個神經元的軸突末端與另一個神經元樹突之間的微小間隙，訊號在這裡以化學方式傳遞——是「神經元之間的接縫」。
ed487e0894c7.en: Synapse: the tiny gap between the axon terminal of one neuron and a dendrite of another neuron, where the signal is passed on chemically. It is the "seam between neurons."

8f10088d1d97.zh: 閾值觸發：發火或不發火
8f10088d1d97.en: Threshold Triggering: Fire or Don't Fire

0df2505d3990.zh: 光知道構造還不夠，關鍵在於機制。當一顆神經元經由樹突與突觸收到鄰居們的訊號後，會在 Soma 裡把這些訊號累積起來。一旦累積的總訊號量超過某個門檻（threshold），神經元就會「發火」（fires）——產生一個沿著軸突（axon）傳遞下去的 action potential（動作電位），把訊息繼續傳給其他神經元；沒超過門檻，就維持沉默。
0df2505d3990.en: Knowing the structure isn't enough; the key is the mechanism. When a neuron receives signals from its neighbors through its dendrites and synapses, it accumulates those signals in the soma. Once the accumulated total signal exceeds a certain threshold, the neuron "fires": it produces an action potential that travels along the axon, passing the message on to other neurons. If the threshold is not exceeded, it stays silent.

20ce384205b0.zh: 這個「超過門檻就開、沒超過就關」的閾值式觸發機制，就是接下來人工神經元模型最核心的靈感來源。
20ce384205b0.en: This threshold-triggered mechanism, "on if the threshold is exceeded, off if not," is the core source of inspiration for the artificial neuron models that come next.

169dee985745.zh: 從生物到抽象：啟發了什麼
169dee985745.en: From Biology to Abstraction: What It Inspired

b3543234d040.zh: 生物神經元「累積訊號 → 超過門檻 → 開關式發火」的流程，被簡化成早期人工神經元的抽象模型：
b3543234d040.en: The biological neuron's flow of "accumulate signals → exceed the threshold → fire like a switch" was simplified into the abstract model of the early artificial neuron:

55f4eb2ba7ca.zh: 把「接收到的多路訊號」想成多個加權輸入；
55f4eb2ba7ca.en: Think of "the multiple incoming signals" as multiple weighted inputs;

041f98411635.zh: 把「累積總量超過門檻」想成加權和過一個閾值；
041f98411635.en: think of "the accumulated total exceeding the threshold" as the weighted sum passing through a threshold;

bc139e5c3415.zh: 把「發火或不發火」想成激活函數輸出 0 或 1。
bc139e5c3415.en: think of "firing or not firing" as the activation function outputting 0 or 1.

c16181d71f64.zh: 也就是說，生物上的「累積 + 閾值 + 開關」，對應到數學上就是「加權和 + 激活」。這顆 1950 年代前就浮現的想法，就是 kp3 的 McCulloch-Pitts 模型的雛形。
c16181d71f64.en: In other words, the biological "accumulation + threshold + switch" corresponds mathematically to "weighted sum + activation." This idea, which surfaced before the 1950s, is the prototype of the McCulloch-Pitts model in KP3.

2123d6d8b13c.zh: 圖 1 生物神經元主要構造（Soma/Dendrites/Synapse）
2123d6d8b13c.en: Figure 1: Main structure of a biological neuron (soma/dendrites/synapse)

191881c16461.zh: 生物神經元：多輸入累積，超過閾值才放電
191881c16461.en: Biological neuron: sums many inputs, fires only above threshold

cd12726a7858.zh: 示意：生物神經元五構造與閾值放電
cd12726a7858.en: Illustration: the five structures of a biological neuron and threshold firing

ac462100dcc3.zh: 🧪 Demo：生物神經元閾值放電 — soma 累積是否超過 θ 觸發動作電位
ac462100dcc3.en: 🧪 Demo: Biological Neuron Threshold Firing — does the soma's accumulated signal exceed θ and trigger an action potential?

d0c14db19be5.zh: 樹突輸入強度 x₁, x₂, x₃（負值為抑制）
d0c14db19be5.en: Dendrite input strengths x₁, x₂, x₃ (negative = inhibitory)

fc91d9137182.zh: soma 累積 z = x₁+x₂+x₃；z 超過 θ 即放電⚡。
fc91d9137182.en: Soma accumulation z = x₁+x₂+x₃; if z exceeds θ, it fires⚡.

67186d035ff3.zh: 三路輸入條 → soma 累積 z（橫軸 0–4）與閾值 θ
67186d035ff3.en: Three input bars → soma accumulation z (horizontal axis 0–4) and threshold θ

55482816dc97.zh: 原理：生物神經元在 soma 累積來自樹突（dendrites）與突觸（synapses）的訊號。 當總輸入超過閾值，神經元就「放電」產生動作電位（action potential）。數學化為：累積值 $z = \sum_{i=1}^{3} x_{i}$，放電條件為 $z > \theta$。輸出 $o$ 為二元步階（Binary Step）： $o = \begin{cases} 1 & z > \theta \quad (\text{放電})\\ 0 & z \le \theta \quad (\text{靜默})\end{cases}$。 調滑桿改變三路輸入強度與閾值，觀察 soma 累積是否跨越 θ 而觸發放電。
55482816dc97.en: Principle: A biological neuron accumulates, in the soma, the signals coming from its dendrites and synapses. When the total input exceeds the threshold, the neuron "fires" and produces an action potential. Written mathematically, the accumulated value is $z = \sum_{i=1}^{3} x_{i}$, and the firing condition is $z > \theta$. The output $o$ is a binary step: $o = \begin{cases} 1 & z > \theta \quad (\text{fire})\\ 0 & z \le \theta \quad (\text{silent})\end{cases}$. Drag the sliders to change the three input strengths and the threshold, and watch whether the soma's accumulated value crosses θ and triggers firing.

25fd09fe40bc.zh: 操作：用滑桿（或直接輸入數值）調整 $x_1, x_2, x_3$ 與閾值 $\theta$。 觀察什麼：累積值 $z = x_1+x_2+x_3$ 是否 $\ge$ θ；超過則閃電⚡放電，否則靜默。 正確基準：readout 中 $z$ 必等於手算 $x_1+x_2+x_3$，放電狀態必等於 $z > \theta$ 的閉式判斷。
25fd09fe40bc.en: How to use: Use the sliders (or type values directly) to adjust $x_1, x_2, x_3$ and the threshold $\theta$. What to watch: whether the accumulated value $z = x_1+x_2+x_3$ is $\ge$ θ; if it is exceeded, a lightning bolt⚡ fires, otherwise it stays silent. Correctness check: the $z$ in the readout must equal $x_1+x_2+x_3$ computed by hand, and the firing state must equal the closed-form test $z > \theta$.

b69771edaa37.zh: McCulloch-Pitts 模型：首個數學神經元
b69771edaa37.en: The McCulloch-Pitts Model: The First Mathematical Neuron

615299c4cde5.zh: 1943 年：第一個把神經元寫成數學的人
615299c4cde5.en: 1943: The First People to Write a Neuron as Math

ec0402c8ff1a.zh: 1943 年，生理學家 Warren McCulloch 與邏輯學家 Walter Pitts 提出了第一個受生物啟發的神經元數學模型，後人稱之為 McCulloch-Pitts neuron。這是人類第一次嘗試把神經計算「形式化」——把神經元的行為用數學規則寫死。
ec0402c8ff1a.en: In 1943, the physiologist Warren McCulloch and the logician Walter Pitts proposed the first biologically inspired mathematical model of a neuron, later known as the McCulloch-Pitts neuron. This was humanity's first attempt to "formalize" neural computation: to hard-code the behavior of a neuron as mathematical rules.

982e5e618f03.zh: 這個模型很簡單，特點如下：
982e5e618f03.en: This model is very simple. Its characteristics are:

c50c8eed8a98.zh: 二元輸入、單一二元輸出：有兩個或以上的二元輸入，產出一個二元輸出（圖見 Fig. 2）。
c50c8eed8a98.en: Binary inputs, a single binary output: it has two or more binary inputs and produces one binary output (see Fig. 2).

bea2efcae5ab.zh: 閾值激活：只有當輸入的「和」超過某個門檻時才會激活（輸出 1），否則維持 0。
bea2efcae5ab.en: Threshold activation: it activates (outputs 1) only when the "sum" of the inputs exceeds a certain threshold; otherwise it stays at 0.

63ab4f969d70.zh: 等權固定：所有輸入被賦予相等且固定的權重。
63ab4f969d70.en: Equal, fixed weights: all inputs are given equal and fixed weights.

24e4595880fe.zh: 無學習：行為完全是預先定義好的，不做任何學習——權重不會更新。
24e4595880fe.en: No learning: its behavior is entirely predefined and it does no learning at all—the weights are never updated.

0ea8f5c56621.zh: 它能做什麼：模擬邏輯閘
0ea8f5c56621.en: What It Can Do: Simulate Logic Gates

765f9a30574e.zh: 因為有「閾值」這個開關，McCulloch-Pitts 神經元可以根據輸入的設定與門檻的高低，模擬基本的邏輯運算，例如 AND、OR、NOT 閘。也就是說，這顆「神經元」其實就像一台小型邏輯電路。
765f9a30574e.en: Because it has the "threshold" switch, a McCulloch-Pitts neuron can simulate basic logical operations, such as AND, OR, and NOT gates, depending on how the inputs are set up and how high the threshold is. In other words, this "neuron" is really like a small logic circuit.

3da3af7415fb.zh: 數學上，這個模型的輸出寫成（式 (1)）：
3da3af7415fb.en: Mathematically, the output of this model is written as (Eq. (1)):

8c4c1876fb72.zh: 神經元先算輸入的加權和，再套上激活函數 $f$，得到輸出 $o$。在 McCulloch-Pitts 模型中，激活函數是二元階梯函數（binary step），所以輸出 $o$ 只取 $\{0,1\}$ 兩個值。
8c4c1876fb72.en: The neuron first computes the weighted sum of its inputs, then applies the activation function $f$ to get the output $o$. In the McCulloch-Pitts model, the activation function is the binary step function, so the output $o$ takes only the two values $\{0,1\}$.

bfa3dc851a4f.zh: 鷹架小結：它教會我們什麼
bfa3dc851a4f.en: Scaffolding Summary: What It Teaches Us

8105c7bbd316.zh: McCulloch-Pitts 把「累積訊號、超過門檻就開」的想法，正式翻譯成「加權和 → 閾值激活」的數學形式。但它有兩個先天限制——權重固定、不能學習。下一節的 Perceptron 正是為了解決「不能學習」這道題而誕生的。
8105c7bbd316.en: McCulloch-Pitts formally translated the idea of "accumulate signals, switch on once the threshold is exceeded" into the mathematical form "weighted sum → threshold activation." But it has two built-in limitations: the weights are fixed, and it cannot learn. The perceptron in the next section was born precisely to solve the "cannot learn" problem.

ee17f8e045ff.zh: Perceptron 與二元激活：第一個會學習的神經元
ee17f8e045ff.en: The Perceptron with Binary Activation: The First Neuron That Learns

70906cafdf60.en: 1958: Rosenblatt Teaches the Neuron to "Correct Its Mistakes"

7184001715e5.zh: McCulloch-Pitts 模型有個致命傷——不能學習。1958 年，生理學家 Frank Rosenblatt 在 Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory 提出並實作了一台機器：Perceptron。它不只模仿神經元的結構，更重要的是引入了一條監督式學習規則來調整權重。Rosenblatt 的目標，是做出能模仿人類視覺感知的系統——今天，Perceptron 被公認是現代神經網路的奠基積木。
7184001715e5.en: The McCulloch-Pitts model has a fatal flaw—it cannot learn. In 1958, the physiologist Frank Rosenblatt, at the Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory, proposed and built a machine: the Perceptron. It did not just imitate the structure of a neuron; more importantly, it introduced a supervised learning rule to adjust the weights. Rosenblatt's goal was to build a system that could imitate human visual perception—today, the Perceptron is widely recognized as the foundational building block of modern neural networks.

1c5b56d28929.zh: 它有幾個值得記住的背景：
1c5b56d28929.en: A few points of background are worth remembering:

cf3f7fda3492.zh: 二元分類：Perceptron 主要為二元分類設計，這既實用、又正好與數位電腦的二元邏輯契合；就算是多類別問題，也能拆成一堆二元子問題。
cf3f7fda3492.en: Binary classification: The Perceptron was designed mainly for binary classification, which is both practical and a natural fit for the binary logic of digital computers; even a multi-class problem can be broken down into a set of binary subproblems.

ef9a243eda0e.zh: 隨機連接：Rosenblatt 最初的設計強調輸入與輸出神經元之間的隨機連接，因為他相信人類視網膜與視覺皮層是隨機連接的。
ef9a243eda0e.en: Random connections: Rosenblatt's original design emphasized random connections between the input and output neurons, because he believed the human retina and visual cortex are randomly connected.

dd51c6dd01dc.zh: Hebbian 啟發但本質不同：早期靈感來自 Hebbian learning（重複共同激發會增強突觸權重），但 Perceptron 最終採用的是一條監督式學習規則——由帶標籤的資料與分類錯誤驅動，這與古典 Hebbian 學習本質上不同。
dd51c6dd01dc.en: Inspired by Hebb, but fundamentally different: The early inspiration came from Hebbian learning (repeated joint firing strengthens synaptic weights), but the Perceptron ultimately adopted a supervised learning rule—driven by labeled data and classification errors, which is fundamentally different from classical Hebbian learning.

c1fec76dd36e.zh: 當年它還上了新聞。1958 年美國海軍的一場記者會上，Rosenblatt 形容 Perceptron 是智慧機器的可能基礎；之後《紐約時報》甚至宣稱它是「一個能走路、說話、看見、書寫、自我複製、且意識到自己存在的電子電腦之胚胎」。這些誇張說法，既帶來了公眾的興奮，也埋下了日後的懷疑。
c1fec76dd36e.en: It even made the news back then. At a 1958 U.S. Navy press conference, Rosenblatt described the Perceptron as a possible foundation for intelligent machines; afterwards, The New York Times went so far as to call it "the embryo of an electronic computer that will be able to walk, talk, see, write, reproduce itself and be conscious of its existence." These exaggerated claims brought public excitement, but also sowed the seeds of later skepticism.

75562782f0c5.en: The structure of the Perceptron is shown in the figure (Fig. 3): it takes a linear combination of the inputs and then feeds it into the activation function $f$. The data are represented as follows—there are $n$ input vectors, and the $i$-th one is written as:

d54d0a851207.en: where $x_{i j}$ is the $j$-th element of the $i$-th data point, and each data point has a corresponding true label $y_{i}$.

ee851de24f2f.zh: 學習規則：錯了就改，對了就停
ee851de24f2f.en: Learning Rule: Fix It When It's Wrong, Stop When It's Right

39703ad85726.zh: 對每一筆資料 $\boldsymbol{x}_{i}$，Perceptron 算出輸出 $o_{i}$，和真實標籤 $y_{i}$ 比較，再依兩者的差來更新權重。權重與偏置的更新規則（式 (2)）是：
39703ad85726.en: For each data point $\boldsymbol{x}_{i}$, the Perceptron computes the output $o_{i}$, compares it with the true label $y_{i}$, and then updates the weights according to the difference between the two. The update rule for the weights and bias (Eq. (2)) is:

700ba11e247d.zh: 用 $x_{i 0}:=1$ 把偏置併進去，就濃縮成式 (3)：
700ba11e247d.en: Using $x_{i 0}:=1$ to absorb the bias, this condenses into Eq. (3):

ba8aced17e10.zh: 其中 $\eta\gt 0$ 是學習率，$y_{i}\in\{0,1\}$ 是真實標籤，$o_{i}$ 是預測輸出。
ba8aced17e10.en: where $\eta\gt 0$ is the learning rate, $y_{i}\in\{0,1\}$ is the true label, and $o_{i}$ is the predicted output.

a87f576dd8c9.zh: batch 版與單樣本版的等價：也可以一次吃一整個 batch 再更新（式 (4)）：
a87f576dd8c9.en: Equivalence of the batch version and the single-sample version: We can also take in a whole batch at once and then update (Eq. (4)):

4ccf9e7da296.zh: 其中 $b$ 是 batch size。去掉求和符號，就回到每次只處理單一樣本的式 (5)：
4ccf9e7da296.en: where $b$ is the batch size. Removing the summation brings us back to Eq. (5), which processes only a single sample at a time:

e66c16d99802.zh: 直覺：如果預測對了，$o_{i}=y_{i}$，那麼 $y_{i}-o_{i}=0$，權重完全不用更新；只有預測錯（差 $\neq 0$）時，權重才會按錯誤大小成比例地往正確方向調整。
e66c16d99802.en: Intuition: If the prediction is correct, $o_{i}=y_{i}$, so $y_{i}-o_{i}=0$ and the weights do not need to be updated at all; only when the prediction is wrong (difference $\neq 0$) are the weights adjusted toward the correct direction, in proportion to the size of the error.

2e68b83500ae.zh: 一句話總結這顆神經元：它比 M-P 模型多了「會看錯誤、會改自己」的能力。把每個樣本送進去，比對「我猜的」和「正確的」，猜錯就照著誤差把權重推一把，猜對就原地不動——這就是監督學習最早的雛形。也正因為它會學習，才值得被稱為現代深度學習的真正起點。
2e68b83500ae.en: To sum up this neuron in one sentence: compared with the M-P model, it gains the ability to "look at its errors and correct itself." Feed in each sample, compare "what I guessed" with "what is correct"; if the guess is wrong, give the weights a push according to the error, and if it is right, stay put—this is the earliest prototype of supervised learning. And precisely because it can learn, it deserves to be called the true starting point of modern deep learning.

1e288a7848ef.zh: 原理：Perceptron 用二元步階當激活，輸出 $o_i \in \{0,1\}$。錯誤 $\delta_i = y_i - o_i$ 驅動學習， 單樣本更新是 $w := w + \eta(y_i-o_i)\,x_i$、$w_0 := w_0 + \eta(y_i-o_i)$（式 2/5）； batch 一次累加整批：$w := w + \eta\sum_{i=1}^{b}(y_i-o_i)\,x_i$（式 4）。 關鍵直覺：預測對了 $y_i=o_i \Rightarrow \delta_i=0$，權重完全不動；只有錯分時才按 $\eta\delta_i x_i$ 把 $w$ 往正確方向推一把。
1e288a7848ef.en: Principle: The Perceptron uses a binary step as its activation, with output $o_i \in \{0,1\}$. The error $\delta_i = y_i - o_i$ drives learning; the single-sample update is $w := w + \eta(y_i-o_i)\,x_i$, $w_0 := w_0 + \eta(y_i-o_i)$ (Eq. 2/5); the batch version accumulates the whole batch at once: $w := w + \eta\sum_{i=1}^{b}(y_i-o_i)\,x_i$ (Eq. 4). Key intuition: when the prediction is correct, $y_i=o_i \Rightarrow \delta_i=0$, and the weights do not move at all; only on a misclassification does $\eta\delta_i x_i$ give $w$ a push toward the correct direction.

a5a92e311042.zh: 操作：調 η（學習率）控制每次步伐大小；切換「單點／batch」更新模式。按「▸ 單步更新」走一步： 單點模式只對第 1 個誤分樣本做式(2)；batch 模式一次對所有誤分樣本做式(4)（錯誤全部先在同一組權重下算好）。 「⏩ 迭代 ×10」連走 10 步；「✋ 手算一步」把 $\Delta w = \eta(y_i-o_i)x_i$ 逐分量展開、給出閉式基準；「↺ 重置權重」回到初始值。 觀察什麼：紅點（誤分）才帶動箭頭 $\Delta w$；正確的綠點使 $\delta=0$、完全不更新；batch 的總 $\Delta w$ 恰為各誤分樣本 $\Delta w$ 的向量和（疊加）。 正確基準：readout 的 $\Delta w$ 值與「手算一步」的閉式 $\eta(y_i-o_i)x_i$ 完全一致。
a5a92e311042.en: How to use: Adjust η (the learning rate) to control the size of each step; switch between the "single point / batch" update modes. Press "▸ Single-step update" to take one step: single-point mode applies Eq. (2) only to the first misclassified sample; batch mode applies Eq. (4) to all misclassified samples at once (all the errors are computed first under the same set of weights). "⏩ Iterate ×10" takes 10 steps in a row; "✋ Compute one step by hand" expands $\Delta w = \eta(y_i-o_i)x_i$ component by component and gives the closed-form reference; "↺ Reset weights" returns to the initial values. What to observe: Only the red points (misclassified) drive the arrow $\Delta w$; the correct green points give $\delta=0$ and cause no update at all; the total $\Delta w$ of a batch is exactly the vector sum (superposition) of the $\Delta w$ of each misclassified sample. Correctness check: The $\Delta w$ values in the readout match the closed-form $\eta(y_i-o_i)x_i$ from "Compute one step by hand" exactly.

4754052b7fda.zh: kp5 (badge 2.5) Signum 激活的 Perceptron：更新規則與兩種推導
4754052b7fda.en: kp5 (badge 2.5) The Perceptron with Signum Activation: The Update Rule and Two Derivations

c7aca47fcbf3.zh: 一、是什麼：把二元步階換成符號函數
c7aca47fcbf3.en: 1. What it is: replacing the binary step with the sign function

28be1e1fabb5.zh: 上一節的 Perceptron 用二元步階（Binary Step）當激活，輸出只有 0 或 1。這一節我們把它換成 signum（符號）函數：輸出變成 +1 或 −1，也就是讓類別標籤直接「有正負之分」。這樣一來，標籤 yi ∈ {+1, −1}，更新規則可以寫得更漂亮。
28be1e1fabb5.en: The perceptron in the previous section used the binary step as its activation, so the output was only 0 or 1. In this section we replace it with the signum (sign) function: the output becomes +1 or −1, which means the class labels themselves now "have a sign." This way, the labels are yi ∈ {+1, −1}, and the update rule can be written more elegantly.

636efb0a7a8c.zh: 二、為什麼：錯誤的修正要「往正確方向推一把」
636efb0a7a8c.en: 2. Why: correcting an error means "giving it a push in the right direction"

d30053766f1b.zh: 還記得二元版本的更新嗎？w := w + η (yi − oi) xi。當輸出用 ±1 表示時，正確與錯誤只分兩種：標籤跟輸出一樣（yi = oi），或標籤跟輸出相反（yi ≠ oi）。於是可以把「對或錯」寫進一個判別條件，得到更新規則 (6) 與 (7)：
d30053766f1b.en: Remember the update for the binary version? w := w + η (yi − oi) xi. When outputs are expressed as ±1, there are only two kinds of right and wrong: the label equals the output (yi = oi), or the label is the opposite of the output (yi ≠ oi). So we can write "right or wrong" into a single condition and obtain update rules (6) and (7):

f780e96c019a.zh: 權重：w := w + 2η yi xi，若 oi ≠ yi；否則不動。
f780e96c019a.en: Weights: w := w + 2η yi xi if oi ≠ yi; otherwise unchanged.

b57b5b7115a0.zh: 偏置：w0 := w0 + 2η yi，若 oi ≠ yi；否則不動。
b57b5b7115a0.en: Bias: w0 := w0 + 2η yi if oi ≠ yi; otherwise unchanged.

83c36ae5937a.zh: 係數「2」不是魔法，它是 yi − oi 在 ±1 反號時必然等於 ±2 的自然結果（下面推導會看到）。批處理（batch）時把所有樣本的修正累加，用指示函數 I(oi ≠ yi) 當「開關」：w := w + 2η Σi=1..b yi xi I(oi ≠ yi)（式 8），偏置同理（式 9）。
83c36ae5937a.en: The coefficient "2" is not magic; it is the natural consequence of yi − oi necessarily equaling ±2 when the two ±1 values have opposite signs (you will see this in the derivation below). In batch mode, the corrections from all samples are summed, using the indicator function I(oi ≠ yi) as a "switch": w := w + 2η Σi=1..b yi xi I(oi ≠ yi) (Eq. 8), and likewise for the bias (Eq. 9).

642d0b80a27b.zh: 三、第一種推導：代數化簡（四種情況全列出）
642d0b80a27b.en: 3. First derivation: algebraic simplification (listing all four cases)

b56b197d6ea8.zh: 從原更新 w := w + η(yi − oi) xi 出發，yi, oi ∈ {−1, 1} 只有四種組合：
b56b197d6ea8.en: Starting from the original update w := w + η(yi − oi) xi, with yi, oi ∈ {−1, 1} there are only four combinations:

aff4efead952.zh: 可以看到：只要 oi ≠ yi，η(yi − oi) xi = 2ηyixi，這就完整推出 (6)(7)(8)(9)。
aff4efead952.en: We can see that whenever oi ≠ yi, η(yi − oi) xi = 2ηyixi, which fully derives (6)(7)(8)(9).

8ccc01f6bdf5.zh: 四、第二種推導：梯度上升／下降的幾何直覺
8ccc01f6bdf5.en: 4. Second derivation: the geometric intuition of gradient ascent/descent

fb97c76ef825.zh: 決策邊界是一條直線（在 Rd 是超平面）：wT x + w0 = 0（式 10）。因為邊界上兩點都滿足此式，相減得 wT(x1 − x2) = 0，所以 w 是決策邊界的法向量（normal vector）（式 11、Fig.5）。
fb97c76ef825.en: The decision boundary is a line (a hyperplane in Rd): wT x + w0 = 0 (Eq. 10). Since any two points on the boundary satisfy this equation, subtracting gives wT(x1 − x2) = 0, so w is the normal vector of the decision boundary (Eq. 11, Fig.5).

1f8c89d04c40.zh: 取邊界上一點 x0，任一點 x 到邊界的距離，在 w 為單位向量時是 d = wT(x − x0) = wTx + w0（式 12）。距離該非負，所以取絕對值 d = |wTx + w0|——但絕對值不平滑、不可微，無法梯度優化。破解法是「用標籤去掉絕對值」：若 y=+1 則 wTx + w0 > 0，若 y=−1 則 < 0（式 13），因此對正確分類的點恆有 d := y(wTx + w0) ≥ 0（式 14）。
1f8c89d04c40.en: Take a point x0 on the boundary; when w is a unit vector, the distance from any point x to the boundary is d = wT(x − x0) = wTx + w0 (Eq. 12). A distance should be non-negative, so we take the absolute value d = |wTx + w0|, but the absolute value is not smooth and not differentiable, so it cannot be optimized with gradients. The trick is to "use the label to remove the absolute value": if y=+1 then wTx + w0 > 0, and if y=−1 then it is < 0 (Eq. 13), so for correctly classified points we always have d := y(wTx + w0) ≥ 0 (Eq. 14).

70113dc289a4.en: The two objectives lead to the same place:

61c442597979.zh: 最大化「正確分類點」的距離（梯度上升）：distance = Σ yi(wTxi + w0)，梯度是 ∂distance/∂w = Σ yixi，於是 w := w + η Σ yixi（式 15）。
61c442597979.en: Maximize the distance of "correctly classified points" (gradient ascent): distance = Σ yi(wTxi + w0), whose gradient is ∂distance/∂w = Σ yixi, so w := w + η Σ yixi (Eq. 15).

ce2229d17e08.zh: 最小化「錯誤分類點」的距離（梯度下降）：把正確點的距離乘 −1 得 error = −Σ yi(wTxi + w0)，梯度下降仍得 w := w + η Σ yixi（式 16）。
ce2229d17e08.en: Minimize the distance of "misclassified points" (gradient descent): multiplying the correct points' distance by −1 gives error = −Σ yi(wTxi + w0), and gradient descent still gives w := w + η Σ yixi (Eq. 16).

393161ef3d7b.zh: 兩條路都給出同一個更新規則，且只要對「錯分」（oi ≠ yi）的樣本做，就回到 (8)(9)。Fig.6 把「w 是法向量、點到線的距離」畫得清清楚楚，是這套幾何直覺的核心。整體思路就是 (10)→(16)：定義邊界→證明法向量→算距離→去掉絕對值→梯度上升/下降。
393161ef3d7b.en: Both routes give the same update rule, and as long as it is applied only to "misclassified" samples (oi ≠ yi), we are back to (8)(9). Fig.6 draws "w is the normal vector, and the distance from a point to the line" very clearly; it is the core of this geometric intuition. The overall line of reasoning is (10)→(16): define the boundary → prove the normal vector → compute the distance → remove the absolute value → gradient ascent/descent.

ac8d414d75b7.zh: ✓ 最終更新公式一致性：代數路徑（式5→6/7）得「錯分時 w := w + 2ηyᵢxᵢ」；幾何路徑（梯度上升式15／梯度下降式16）得「錯分時 w := w + ηΣyᵢxᵢ，僅對 oᵢ≠yᵢ 樣本做」——兩路都收斂到同一個更新規則，即 batch 指示函數版式(8)(9)。
ac8d414d75b7.en: ✓ Consistency of the final update formula: the algebraic path (Eq. 5→6/7) gives "when misclassified, w := w + 2ηyᵢxᵢ"; the geometric path (gradient ascent Eq. 15 / gradient descent Eq. 16) gives "when misclassified, w := w + ηΣyᵢxᵢ, applied only to samples with oᵢ≠yᵢ"; both paths converge to the same update rule, namely the batch indicator-function version, Eqs. (8)(9).

7af8a8fe01d9.zh: 原理：換成 signum 激活後 $y_i,o_i \in \{-1,1\}$，原更新 $w := w + \eta(y_i-o_i)\,x_i$（式 5）只剩四種情況： $o_i=y_i$ 時 $\eta(y_i-o_i)x_i=\mathbf{0}$，$o_i\ne y_i$ 時 $=\pm 2\eta x_i = 2\eta y_i x_i$（式 6/7）；batch 版用指示函數 $\mathbb{I}(o_i\ne y_i)$ 當開關（式 8/9）。 幾何路徑：決策邊界 $w^{\top}x+w_0=0$（式 10），因邊界上兩點相減 $w^{\top}(x_1-x_2)=0$ 所以 $w$ 是法向量；距離以 $d := y(w^{\top}x+w_0)$（式 14）去絕對值，梯度上升（式 15）與下降（式 16）殊途同歸。
7af8a8fe01d9.en: Principle: after switching to the signum activation, $y_i,o_i \in \{-1,1\}$, and the original update $w := w + \eta(y_i-o_i)\,x_i$ (Eq. 5) reduces to just four cases: when $o_i=y_i$, $\eta(y_i-o_i)x_i=\mathbf{0}$; when $o_i\ne y_i$, it is $=\pm 2\eta x_i = 2\eta y_i x_i$ (Eq. 6/7); the batch version uses the indicator function $\mathbb{I}(o_i\ne y_i)$ as a switch (Eq. 8/9). The geometric path: the decision boundary is $w^{\top}x+w_0=0$ (Eq. 10); subtracting two points on the boundary gives $w^{\top}(x_1-x_2)=0$, so $w$ is the normal vector; the distance $d := y(w^{\top}x+w_0)$ (Eq. 14) removes the absolute value, and gradient ascent (Eq. 15) and gradient descent (Eq. 16) lead to the same place.

da78f5fa3b46.zh: 操作：切換「代數視角／幾何視角」兩頁籤。 代數頁：選 yᵢ、oᵢ 四組合之一，看 $\eta(y_i-o_i)x_i$ 化簡成 $\mathbf{0}$ 或 $2\eta y_i x_i$（上表同步標出該列）；η 改變步伐。 幾何頁：調 w₁、w₂、w₀ 移動決策邊界，拖曳樣本點 x、切換標籤 y——綠色箭頭是法向量 $w$（垂直邊界），點依 $d=y(w^{\top}x+w_0)$ 著色（≥0 綠＝正確、<0 紅＝誤分），readout 給出距離數值。 正確基準：代數頁每列的化簡與式(6)一致（$o_i\ne y_i \Rightarrow 2\eta y_i x_i$）；幾何頁 $d$ 值即閉式 $y(w^{\top}x+w_0)$；兩頁最終更新公式都指向 $w+2\eta y_i x_i$（一致性標記為綠）。
da78f5fa3b46.en: How to use: switch between the two tabs, "Algebraic view / Geometric view." Algebraic tab: pick one of the four combinations of yᵢ, oᵢ and watch $\eta(y_i-o_i)x_i$ simplify to $\mathbf{0}$ or $2\eta y_i x_i$ (the table above highlights that row at the same time); η changes the step size. Geometric tab: adjust w₁, w₂, w₀ to move the decision boundary, drag the sample point x, and toggle the label y. The green arrow is the normal vector $w$ (perpendicular to the boundary), the point is colored by $d=y(w^{\top}x+w_0)$ (≥0 green = correct, <0 red = misclassified), and the readout gives the distance value. Correctness check: on the algebraic tab, each row's simplification agrees with Eq. (6) ($o_i\ne y_i \Rightarrow 2\eta y_i x_i$); on the geometric tab, the $d$ value is exactly the closed form $y(w^{\top}x+w_0)$; on both tabs the final update formula points to $w+2\eta y_i x_i$ (the consistency marker is green).

400974009128.en: In the perceptron with signum activation, what values can the output o_i take?

2da70ec99b59.en: When y_i,o_i ∈ {−1,1} and the classification is wrong (o_i≠y_i), what does η(y_i−o_i)x_i simplify to?

5b8dd6b72a9a.en: Why rewrite the distance d=|w^T x+w_0| as d:=y(w^T x+w_0)?

852c72bbfe29.en: The absolute value is not differentiable; the rewritten form is always non-negative and differentiable

55cb9358b5cc.en: They differ by a minus sign

4aaef2d056ae.zh: kp6 (badge 2.6) Perceptron 的限制：XOR 反例與泛化問題
4aaef2d056ae.en: kp6 (badge 2.6) Limitations of the Perceptron: The XOR Counterexample and the Generalization Problem

83659fa1e854.zh: 一、是什麼：Perceptron 天生只能做「線性可分」
83659fa1e854.en: 1. What it is: the perceptron can only handle "linearly separable" problems by nature

1c301fa505f1.zh: Perceptron 的決策邊界是一條直線（或超平面），所以它只適合「二元分類 + 資料線性可分」的問題。一旦資料需要彎曲的邊界，它就無能為力。
1c301fa505f1.en: The perceptron's decision boundary is a straight line (or hyperplane), so it is only suited to problems that are "binary classification + linearly separable data." As soon as the data needs a curved boundary, it is helpless.

b5b78e36867d.zh: 二、為什麼：Minsky & Papert 的 XOR 反例與「寒冬」
b5b78e36867d.en: 2. Why: Minsky & Papert's XOR counterexample and the "winter"

99e65acb3cfc.zh: 1969 年，Minsky 與 Papert 在經典著作 Perceptrons 中嚴格證明：Perceptron 無法處理需要非線性決策邊界的問題，最著名的反例就是 XOR（異或）。XOR 的四個輸入點，+1 與 −1 兩類交叉分佈，任一條直線都無法把它們分開，而 Perceptron 的邊界偏偏是直線。這個打擊讓神經網路研究熱情「急凍」了許多年——史稱神經網路的第一次寒冬。
99e65acb3cfc.en: In 1969, Minsky and Papert rigorously proved in their classic book Perceptrons that the perceptron cannot handle problems that require a non-linear decision boundary; the most famous counterexample is XOR (exclusive OR). XOR's four input points have the two classes, +1 and −1, arranged in a crisscross, so no single straight line can separate them, and the perceptron's boundary happens to be exactly a straight line. This blow "froze" enthusiasm for neural network research for many years—what history calls the first winter of neural networks.

1e26f4113629.zh: 當時大家其實已猜測「把多個 Perceptron 堆疊成多層架構」或許能繞過非線性限制，但沒有高效率的訓練演算法，多層網路不知道該怎麼學，進展因此停滯。
1e26f4113629.en: At the time, people had in fact already guessed that "stacking multiple perceptrons into a multilayer architecture" might get around the non-linearity limitation, but there was no efficient training algorithm: nobody knew how a multilayer network should learn, so progress stalled.

0f85a86ed9fc.zh: 三、怎麼用：即使線性可分，泛化也很差
0f85a86ed9fc.en: 3. How it's used: even when the data is linearly separable, generalization is poor

d4bf0e9611f4.zh: 別以為資料可分就萬事大吉。Perceptron 的最終邊界取決於隨機初始權重：初始值不同，收斂到的決策邊界就不同（Fig.7a）。有些邊界會「貼著某一類資料」劃過去（Fig.7b），雖然在訓練集上準確率 100%，對沒見過的新資料卻常常誤判——也就是泛化能力差。
d4bf0e9611f4.en: Don't think that separable data means everything is fine. The perceptron's final boundary depends on the random initial weights: different initial values converge to different decision boundaries (Fig.7a). Some boundaries pass "hugging one of the classes" (Fig.7b); although they reach 100% accuracy on the training set, they often misclassify new data they have never seen—that is, poor generalization.

f524fc67fa9f.zh: 四、對策：ADALINE 登場，但非線性才是王道
f524fc67fa9f.en: 4. The remedy: ADALINE enters the stage, but non-linearity is king

029a2d73e41a.zh: 為了改善泛化、並處理不可分的資料，Widrow 與 Hoff 在 1960 年提出 ADALINE（Adaptive Linear Neuron）。它改用 LMS（Least Mean Squares）演算法最小化一個連續的損失函數（不像 Perceptron 的「錯分個數」是離散的），因此收斂更穩定、泛化更好。
029a2d73e41a.en: To improve generalization and to handle non-separable data, Widrow and Hoff proposed ADALINE (Adaptive Linear Neuron) in 1960. Instead, it uses the LMS (least mean squares) algorithm to minimize a continuous loss function (unlike the perceptron's "number of misclassifications," which is discrete), so it converges more stably and generalizes better.

245f495dc4ef.zh: 但 ADALINE 並未成為深度學習的基石——它的線性輸出不適合深層架構所需的階層式非線性特徵表示。反觀 Perceptron，正因為它有非線性激活，才適合當作多層網路的基本單位。所以結論是：Perceptron 的非線性激活，才是現代神經網路的雛形；ADALINE 的故事留在 §3 詳細講。
245f495dc4ef.en: But ADALINE did not become the cornerstone of deep learning—its linear output is not suited to the hierarchical non-linear feature representations that deep architectures need. The perceptron, by contrast, is suited to being the basic unit of a multilayer network precisely because it has a non-linear activation. So the conclusion is: the perceptron's non-linear activation is the prototype of modern neural networks; the ADALINE story is told in detail in §3.

b93b865be3e8.zh:
線性邊界：Perceptron 的決策面是一條直線（超平面），寫成 $w^{\top}x + w_{0}=0$。把輸出規則（二元階梯）寫清楚： $$\hat{y}=\begin{cases}1 & w^{\top}x + w_{0} > 0\\0 & w^{\top}x + w_{0} \le 0\end{cases}$$ 所以 單層 Perceptron 只解得了「線性可分」 的問題。

XOR 為何不可分：四個點 (0,0)、(1,0)、(0,1)、(1,1) 中，同標籤落在對角線兩端 （(0,0),(1,1) 為類 0；(1,0),(0,1) 為類 1）， 需要「彎曲」的邊界。任一直線 $w^{\top}x+w_{0}=0$ 一定把某顆同標籤的點分到另一側。
b93b865be3e8.en:
Linear boundary: the perceptron's decision surface is a straight line (hyperplane), written as $w^{\top}x + w_{0}=0$. Writing out the output rule (binary step) explicitly: $$\hat{y}=\begin{cases}1 & w^{\top}x + w_{0} > 0\\0 & w^{\top}x + w_{0} \le 0\end{cases}$$ So a single-layer perceptron can only solve "linearly separable" problems.

Why XOR is not separable: among the four points (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1), points with the same label sit at the two ends of a diagonal ((0,0),(1,1) are class 0; (1,0),(0,1) are class 1), which needs a "curved" boundary. Any straight line $w^{\top}x+w_{0}=0$ is bound to put one of the same-label points on the other side.

a9ca7ae63e69.zh: 理論基準：對 XOR 四點，任何 (m,b) 的誤分數 ≥ 1（最佳也只能對 3/4）； 而「線性可分」資料集存在誤分數為 0 的直線。
a9ca7ae63e69.en: Theoretical baseline: for the four XOR points, the number of misclassifications for any (m,b) is ≥ 1 (the best you can do is get 3/4 right); whereas for a "linearly separable" dataset there exists a line with 0 misclassifications.

c172ae9e6bbd.zh: 操作：用「斜率 m」「截距 b」兩條滑桿轉動那條直線，試著讓它把所有點分開—— 在 XOR 模式下無論你怎麼調，誤分數永遠 ≥ 1（錯誤的點會閃爍）， 這就是 Minsky & Papert（1969）證明「單層 Perceptron 解不了 XOR」的直觀原因。 點開 「線性可分」 切換鈕，換成兩群可分離的點，誤分數就能降到 0（可分）。 也可以拖動點或按「🎲 亂擺一點試試」，觀察：把點稍微移開標準 XOR 位置後， 只要還維持「對角同類」的錯開排列，直線依然分不開。 看什麼：閃爍 = 誤分；讀出的 wᵀx+w₀=0 與滑桿的 y=mx+b 是完全同一條線。
c172ae9e6bbd.en: How to use: use the two sliders, "slope m" and "intercept b," to turn the line and try to make it separate all the points— in XOR mode, no matter how you adjust it, the number of misclassifications is always ≥ 1 (the wrong points flash); this is the intuitive reason behind Minsky & Papert's (1969) proof that "a single-layer perceptron can't solve XOR." Click the "Linearly separable" toggle to switch to two separable groups of points, and the number of misclassifications can drop to 0 (separable). You can also drag the points or press "🎲 Try a random point," and observe: after moving the points slightly away from the standard XOR positions, as long as they keep the staggered "same class on the diagonal" arrangement, a line still can't separate them. What to look for: flashing = misclassified; the readout wᵀx+w₀=0 and the sliders' y=mx+b are exactly the same line.

e810319e5bd3.zh: 單一 Perceptron 只能畫直線，那多放幾個、疊成多層呢？這就引出 多層感知機 MLP（Multi-Layer Perceptron）——它由 Rosenblatt 在 1958 年（和 Perceptron 同一篇論文）提出。關鍵限制是當時沒有訓練演算法，直到 反向傳播（backpropagation） 出現，多層網路才真正能學、深度學習的時代才開啟。
e810319e5bd3.en: A single perceptron can only draw a straight line, so what if we put in several and stack them into multiple layers? This leads to the multilayer perceptron (MLP)—proposed by Rosenblatt in 1958 (in the same paper as the perceptron). The key limitation was that there was no training algorithm at the time; only when backpropagation appeared could multilayer networks really learn, and the era of deep learning begin.

3aacfc32d64a.zh: 二、為什麼：feedforward / fully-connected / dense 是同義詞
3aacfc32d64a.en: 2. Why: feedforward / fully-connected / dense are synonyms

50ad07a1b448.zh: 這種網路叫 feedforward（前饋），因為資訊只向前傳、不回頭。在每一層，前一層的所有神經元都連到下一層的所有神經元，所以又叫 fully-connected（全連接）；每一層就叫 fully connected layer 或 dense layer（密集層）。而每一顆神經元都是一個 Perceptron 神經元——這正是「多層感知機」名字的由來。
50ad07a1b448.en: This kind of network is called feedforward, because information only flows forward and never goes back. In each layer, every neuron of the previous layer is connected to every neuron of the next layer, so it is also called fully-connected; each layer is called a fully connected layer or dense layer. And every neuron is a perceptron neuron—which is exactly where the name "multilayer perceptron" comes from.

b082177e665e.zh: 四、神經元內部：兩步「先線性、後非線性」
b082177e665e.en: 4. Inside a neuron: two steps, "linear first, then non-linear"

c5d02ac5367f.zh: 每一顆神經元都是 Perceptron（見 Fig.9），內部分兩步：
c5d02ac5367f.en: Every neuron is a perceptron (see Fig.9), and internally it works in two steps:

8bad421bee58.zh:
線性加總（式 17）：把上一層的輸出 zℓ 各自乘上權重 wiℓ 再加起來：
ai = Σℓ=1..m wiℓ zℓ，其中 m 是上一層神經元數。
8bad421bee58.en:
Linear summation (Eq. 17): multiply each output zℓ of the previous layer by its weight wiℓ and add them up:
ai = Σℓ=1..m wiℓ zℓ, where m is the number of neurons in the previous layer.

b76e117f1d4c.zh:
非線性激活（式 18）：把 ai 丟進激活函數 σi(·)（通常非線性）：
zi := σi(ai)。
b76e117f1d4c.en:
Non-linear activation (Eq. 18): feed ai into the activation function σi(·) (usually non-linear):
zi := σi(ai).

dac5a21edaf1.zh: 一句話總結：神經元 = 權重加總 + 非線性激活，而整個網路就是把這「先線性、後非線性」的步驟一層一層疊起來，前饋地從輸入流向輸出。
dac5a21edaf1.en: In one sentence: neuron = weighted sum + non-linear activation, and the whole network just stacks this "linear first, then non-linear" step layer by layer, flowing feedforward from input to output.

6ada68477af1.zh: 這一節要回答一個「看似簡單、其實關鍵」的問題：為什麼神經網路一定要有非線性的激活函數？直接給你結論——如果所有激活都是線性的，那不管疊幾層，整座網路最終都坍縮成一次線性投影，等於只是一個更胖的線性模型，完全失去「深」的意義。
6ada68477af1.en: This section answers a question that "looks simple but is actually crucial": why must a neural network have non-linear activation functions? Here's the conclusion up front: if every activation is linear, then no matter how many layers you stack, the whole network ultimately collapses into a single linear projection, which amounts to just a fatter linear model, and it completely loses the point of being "deep".

c06f51d9b7a2.en: What one layer looks like: linear projection + activation

25a4078e2b37.zh: 回顧上一節，每一層的運算都是「先把輸入做線性投影，再套上激活函數」。把三層串起來，整座網路的輸出可以寫成（注意每個 \(\sigma\) 包住前一層的結果）：
25a4078e2b37.en: Recall from the previous section that every layer's computation is "first apply a linear projection to the input, then apply the activation function". Chaining three layers together, the output of the whole network can be written as (note that each \(\sigma\) wraps the result of the previous layer):

a55286946c21.zh: 這裡 \(\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\) 就是把輸入 \(\boldsymbol{x}\) 投影到 \(\boldsymbol{W}_i\) 的「行空間」，\(\sigma_i\) 是第 \(i\) 層的激活函數。
a55286946c21.en: Here \(\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\) projects the input \(\boldsymbol{x}\) onto the "column space" of \(\boldsymbol{W}_i\), and \(\sigma_i\) is the activation function of layer \(i\).

39bb4e6229d2.zh: 致命推導：線性激活 ⇒ 網路坍縮
39bb4e6229d2.en: The fatal derivation: linear activations ⇒ the network collapses

95dde93d03c9.zh: 假設每一層的激活函數都是線性的。因為「線性函數 + 線性投影」仍然是線性算子，我們可以把兩者合併成一個新的線性投影 \(\boldsymbol{V}_i:=\sigma_i\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\)。於是上面的式子一步一步變成（推導表）：
95dde93d03c9.en: Suppose every layer's activation function is linear. Because "linear function + linear projection" is still a linear operator, we can merge the two into a new linear projection \(\boldsymbol{V}_i:=\sigma_i\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\). The expression above then turns, step by step, into (derivation table):

08ad21b3845f.zh: \(\sigma_i\) 線性、\(\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\) 線性 ⇒ 令 \(\boldsymbol{V}_i:=\sigma_i\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\) 仍是線性投影
08ad21b3845f.en: \(\sigma_i\) is linear and \(\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\) is linear ⇒ letting \(\boldsymbol{V}_i:=\sigma_i\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\) still gives a linear projection

18586d9df7a7.zh: 其中 \(\boldsymbol{V}:=\boldsymbol{V}_1\boldsymbol{V}_2\boldsymbol{V}_3\) (21)，三個線性矩陣相乘結果仍是一個線性矩陣
18586d9df7a7.en: where \(\boldsymbol{V}:=\boldsymbol{V}_1\boldsymbol{V}_2\boldsymbol{V}_3\) (21); the product of three linear matrices is still a linear matrix

7ba104ce05b5.zh: 結論：\(\boldsymbol{y}\) 只是輸入 \(\boldsymbol{x}\) 的一次線性投影
7ba104ce05b5.en: Conclusion: \(\boldsymbol{y}\) is just a single linear projection of the input \(\boldsymbol{x}\)

e0b4b929e336.zh: 原文 Fig. 10 畫的就是這個概念：把每一層的權重看成夾在激活函數之間的「線性投影矩陣」。如果中間那些激活都是線性的，這些矩陣就會像疊積木一樣直接乘在一起，變成一個大矩陣——你疊了 100 層，數學上卻跟 1 層一樣。
e0b4b929e336.en: Fig. 10 in the source text draws exactly this idea: think of each layer's weights as a "linear projection matrix" sandwiched between activation functions. If the activations in between are all linear, these matrices simply multiply together like stacked building blocks and become one big matrix: you stack 100 layers, yet mathematically it's the same as 1 layer.

98fb317d83fd.zh: 結論：非線性 = 表達能力

42cffca244b5.en: A network can handle non-linear data patterns (such as XOR or curved decision boundaries) precisely because of its non-linear activation functions.

d844fdb8da20.zh: 要讓「深」有意義，就必須在每一層的線性投影之間插入非線性——這也解釋了為什麼下一節要花一整節介紹各種非線性激活函數。
d844fdb8da20.en: For "deep" to mean anything, you must insert a non-linearity between the linear projections of every layer. This also explains why the next section spends an entire section introducing the various non-linear activation functions.

f443612d9b7f.zh: 全線性時三層併成單矩陣 V（式 20/21），決策邊界是一條直線；含 ReLU 時保留下來、邊界會彎曲。
f443612d9b7f.en: When all linear, the three layers merge into a single matrix V (Eq. 20/21) and the decision boundary is a straight line; with ReLU, the layers survive and the boundary bends.

913cae806e1a.zh: 畫布：藍= y>0，橙= y<0，黑線=決策邊界 y=0。重抽權重觀察坍縮與否。
913cae806e1a.en: Canvas: blue = y>0, orange = y<0, black line = decision boundary y=0. Redraw the weights and watch whether it collapses.

148ce2fa7372.zh: 輸入平面 (x₁, x₂) · 3 層網路的輸出 y = W₃ᵀ·σ₂(W₂ᵀ·σ₁(W₁ᵀx))
148ce2fa7372.en: Input plane (x₁, x₂) · output of the 3-layer network y = W₃ᵀ·σ₂(W₂ᵀ·σ₁(W₁ᵀx))

cf71c097372a.zh: 原理：前饋網路每層是「線性投影 + 激活」：$y=\sigma_3\big(W_3^\top \sigma_2(W_2^\top \sigma_1(W_1^\top x))\big)$（式 19）。 若 $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3$ 全為線性，令 $V_i:=\sigma_i W_i^\top$，則各層都是線性算子， 式(19) 化簡為 $y=V_3^\top V_2^\top V_1^\top x=V^\top x$（式 20），其中 $V:=V_1 V_2 V_3$（式 21）——整座網路坍縮成單一線性投影。 決策邊界只能是直線，學不了 XOR 之類非線性模式。反之只要有一層非線性激活（如 ReLU）， 網路就不再等於任何單一矩陣，邊界可以彎曲。關鍵：網路的表達力正是來自非線性激活。
cf71c097372a.en: Principle: Each layer of a feedforward network is "linear projection + activation": $y=\sigma_3\big(W_3^\top \sigma_2(W_2^\top \sigma_1(W_1^\top x))\big)$ (Eq. 19). If $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3$ are all linear, let $V_i:=\sigma_i W_i^\top$; then every layer is a linear operator, and Eq. (19) simplifies to $y=V_3^\top V_2^\top V_1^\top x=V^\top x$ (Eq. 20), where $V:=V_1 V_2 V_3$ (Eq. 21): the whole network collapses into a single linear projection. The decision boundary can only be a straight line, and it cannot learn non-linear patterns such as XOR. Conversely, as long as one layer has a non-linear activation (such as ReLU), the network is no longer equal to any single matrix, and the boundary can bend. Key point: a network's expressive power comes precisely from its non-linear activations.

9d3ddd8c6381.zh: 操作：切換「全線性／含 ReLU」兩種模式，觀察畫布上的決策邊界與 readout 的坍縮判定。 按「🎲 重新抽權重」換一組隨機 $W_1,W_2,W_3$ 再比一次。觀察什麼：全線性模式下，三層前向輸出與坍縮單矩陣 $M=W_3 W_2 W_1$ 的輸出完全一致（max|差|≈0，邊界是直線＝坍縮成立）； 含 ReLU 模式下，前向輸出不再等於 $Mx$（差很大，邊界彎曲＝非線性保留下來）。 正確基準：readout 的全線性等價誤差應為機器精度級（≪10⁻⁶）；非線性誤差應遠大於 0。
9d3ddd8c6381.en: How to use: Switch between the two modes, "All linear / With ReLU", and watch the decision boundary on the canvas and the collapse verdict in the readout. Press "🎲 Redraw weights" to get a new set of random $W_1,W_2,W_3$ and compare again. What to observe: in all-linear mode, the three-layer forward output and the output of the collapsed single matrix $M=W_3 W_2 W_1$ are exactly the same (max|diff|≈0, the boundary is a straight line = the collapse holds); in ReLU mode, the forward output is no longer equal to $Mx$ (a large difference, a curved boundary = the non-linearity survives). Correctness check: the readout's all-linear equivalence error should be at machine-precision level (≪10⁻⁶); the non-linear error should be far greater than 0.

1403fce57739.zh: 如果網路中所有激活函數都是線性的，整座網路會變成？
1403fce57739.en: If all activation functions in a network are linear, what does the whole network become?

ec2f79c756df.zh: 一次線性投影，整體坍縮為線性
ec2f79c756df.en: A single linear projection; the whole thing collapses to linear

382df053802d.zh: 一個指數級複雜的模型

34dbee73bbd3.en: A model that cannot be trained

87af5873f551.zh: 在三層全線性網路中，令 \(\boldsymbol{V}_i:=\sigma_i\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\)，最終 \(\boldsymbol{V}\) 等於？
87af5873f551.en: In a three-layer all-linear network, let \(\boldsymbol{V}_i:=\sigma_i\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\). What does the final \(\boldsymbol{V}\) equal?

ff4367928c46.zh: 網路之所以能處理非線性資料模式（如 XOR），其表達能力來自？
ff4367928c46.en: Where does a network's expressive power to handle non-linear data patterns (such as XOR) come from?

3ffaee676833.en: What is the geometric meaning of \(\boldsymbol{W}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\)?

e066726993bb.zh: 把 \(\boldsymbol{x}\) 投影到 \(\boldsymbol{W}_i\) 的行空間
e066726993bb.en: Projecting \(\boldsymbol{x}\) onto the column space of \(\boldsymbol{W}_i\)

6d05bb1ce4dd.zh: 13 種激活函數一覽：從線性到 maxout
6d05bb1ce4dd.en: An overview of 13 activation functions: from linear to maxout

221d0293d06a.zh: 既然非線性是表達能力的來源，接下來這節把最常用的 13 種激活函數一次看過。每一種你都掌握三件事：公式長什麼樣、輸出的值域在哪、導數是多少（原文 Fig. 11 有完整的圖對照）。先記住一個總原則：輸出值域決定「能不能當機率」「會不會讓梯度消失」。
221d0293d06a.en: Since nonlinearity is the source of expressive power, this section goes through the 13 most commonly used activation functions in one go. For each one, you should master three things: what the formula looks like, what the output range is, and what the derivative is (Fig. 11 in the original text has a complete side-by-side chart). First, remember one general principle: the output range determines "whether it can serve as a probability" and "whether it causes vanishing gradients".

1ce608afd0d4.zh: 基礎款：線性、二元、sign、softmax（當機率用）
1ce608afd0d4.en: The basics: linear, binary, sign, softmax (used as a probability)

d9cefcfa2758.zh: Linear / identity (22)：\(\sigma(a)=a\)，值域 \((-\infty,\infty)\)，\(\sigma'(a)=1\)。等於沒做轉換，幾乎不用在隱藏層，但回歸任務的輸出層可以。注意：若拿它當激活，網路就坍縮回線性。
d9cefcfa2758.en: Linear / identity (22): \(\sigma(a)=a\), range \((-\infty,\infty)\), \(\sigma'(a)=1\). It amounts to no transformation at all; it is almost never used in hidden layers, but it can be used in the output layer for regression tasks. Note: if you use it as the activation, the network collapses back into a linear one.

3f7d2acd2ac6.zh: Binary Step (23)：\(\sigma(a)=0\)（\(a\lt 0\)）／\(1\)（\(a\ge0\)），值域 \([0,1]\)。在 \(a=0\) 處不可導，故現代深度學習少用。
3f7d2acd2ac6.en: Binary Step (23): \(\sigma(a)=0\) (\(a\lt 0\)) / \(1\) (\(a\ge0\)), range \([0,1]\). It is not differentiable at \(a=0\), so it is rarely used in modern deep learning.

459c54fa1bf8.zh: Sign / signum (24)：輸出 \(-1\) 或 \(1\)，值域 \([-1,1]\)。保留輸入的正負號，偶爾用於量化網路。
459c54fa1bf8.en: Sign / signum (24): outputs \(-1\) or \(1\), range \([-1,1]\). It preserves the sign of the input and is occasionally used in quantized networks.

8b51213f8280.zh: Softmax (33)(34)：\(\sigma_i(\boldsymbol{a})=e^{a_i}/\sum_{i=1}^{m}e^{a_i}\)，值域 \((0,1)\) 且跨類別求和為 1。它是 sigmoid 對多分類的推廣，作用在整層（cross-layer），不是逐點；導數含 Kronecker delta：\(\sigma_i(\boldsymbol{a})(\delta_{ij}-\sigma_j(\boldsymbol{a}))\)。
8b51213f8280.en: Softmax (33)(34): \(\sigma_i(\boldsymbol{a})=e^{a_i}/\sum_{i=1}^{m}e^{a_i}\), range \((0,1)\), summing to 1 across classes. It is the generalization of the sigmoid to multi-class classification, and it acts on the whole layer (cross-layer), not element-wise; its derivative contains the Kronecker delta: \(\sigma_i(\boldsymbol{a})(\delta_{ij}-\sigma_j(\boldsymbol{a}))\).

d02627f5c1ab.en: The S-shaped (bounded) kind: sigmoid, tanh, Gaussian

b53adab23536.zh: Logistic / sigmoid (25)：\(\sigma(a)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-a}}\in[0,1]\)，\(\sigma'(a)=\sigma(a)(1-\sigma(a))\)。常當二元分類輸出層的機率；值域可解釋成機率。
b53adab23536.en: Logistic / sigmoid (25): \(\sigma(a)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-a}}\in[0,1]\), \(\sigma'(a)=\sigma(a)(1-\sigma(a))\). It is commonly used as the probability in the output layer for binary classification; its range can be interpreted as a probability.

ef83b4e8c28c.zh: tanh (26)：\(\sigma(a)=\frac{e^a-e^{-a}}{e^a+e^{-a}}\in[-1,1]\)，\(\sigma'(a)=1-\sigma(a)^2\)。跟 sigmoid 很像但輸出零中心，實務上收斂常更快。
ef83b4e8c28c.en: tanh (26): \(\sigma(a)=\frac{e^a-e^{-a}}{e^a+e^{-a}}\in[-1,1]\), \(\sigma'(a)=1-\sigma(a)^2\). Very similar to the sigmoid, but its output is zero-centered, and in practice it often converges faster.

8c2283b3fc64.zh: Gaussian / RBF (27)：\(\sigma(a)=e^{-a^2}\in(0,1]\)，\(\sigma'(a)=-2ae^{-a^2}\)。鐘形，用於 RBF 網路，深度學習少用。
8c2283b3fc64.en: Gaussian / RBF (27): \(\sigma(a)=e^{-a^2}\in(0,1]\), \(\sigma'(a)=-2ae^{-a^2}\). Bell-shaped; used in RBF networks, rarely used in deep learning.

2f5d7123b694.zh: 里程碑款：ReLU 家族（解決梯度消失＋稀疏）
2f5d7123b694.en: The milestone kind: the ReLU family (solves vanishing gradients + sparsity)

2ebc6ad2e79e.zh: Softplus (28)：\(\sigma(a)=\ln(1+e^a)\in[0,\infty)\)，\(\sigma'(a)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-a}}\)。ReLU 的光滑近似，輸出恆正、理論性質好，但收斂常較慢。
2ebc6ad2e79e.en: Softplus (28): \(\sigma(a)=\ln(1+e^a)\in[0,\infty)\), \(\sigma'(a)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-a}}\). A smooth approximation of ReLU; its output is always positive and it has nice theoretical properties, but it often converges more slowly.

8686864764c5.zh: ReLU (29)：\(\sigma(a)=\max(0,a)\in[0,\infty)\)，\(a\gt 0\) 時 \(\sigma'(a)=1\)、\(a\lt 0\) 時為 0。這是深度學習的里程碑：正值段導數恒為 1，避免梯度消失，且把負激發歸零帶來稀疏性、有助泛化。
8686864764c5.en: ReLU (29): \(\sigma(a)=\max(0,a)\in[0,\infty)\), \(\sigma'(a)=1\) when \(a\gt 0\) and 0 when \(a\lt 0\). This is a milestone of deep learning: the derivative is always 1 on the positive part, which avoids vanishing gradients, and zeroing out negative activations brings sparsity, which helps generalization.

060b1757fa7f.zh: dying ReLU 與修補：ReLU 在負區間導數為 0，若神經元老是收到負輸入，權重更新為 0、就「死掉」了。因此有——Leaky ReLU (31)：負區間給小斜率 \(0.01\)，\(\sigma(a)=0.01a\)（\(a\lt 0\)）；PReLU (32)：把負斜率 \(\alpha\) 變成可學習參數，是 Leaky 的一般化。
060b1757fa7f.en: Dying ReLU and its fixes: ReLU's derivative is 0 on the negative interval, so if a neuron keeps receiving negative inputs, its weight updates are 0 and it "dies." Hence we have Leaky ReLU (31): gives the negative interval a small slope \(0.01\), \(\sigma(a)=0.01a\) (\(a\lt 0\)); and PReLU (32): turns the negative slope \(\alpha\) into a learnable parameter, a generalization of Leaky ReLU.

330c3ed29a61.zh: ELU (30)：負區間用 \(\alpha(e^a-1)\) 平滑過渡，輸出 \((-\alpha,\infty)\)，比 ReLU 平滑。
330c3ed29a61.en: ELU (30): uses \(\alpha(e^a-1)\) on the negative interval for a smooth transition, output \((-\alpha,\infty)\), smoother than ReLU.

5c3978cda923.zh: Maxout (35)：\(\sigma_i(\boldsymbol{a})=\max_j(\sigma_j)\)，回傳多個輸入中的最大值，值域 \((-\infty,\infty)\)。具通用近似性質，對 dropout 正規化較穩健；導數在取最大處為 1、其餘為 0。
5c3978cda923.en: Maxout (35): \(\sigma_i(\boldsymbol{a})=\max_j(\sigma_j)\), returns the maximum of several inputs, range \((-\infty,\infty)\). It has the universal approximation property and is more robust with dropout regularization; its derivative is 1 where the maximum is taken and 0 elsewhere.

13de2fff1f10.zh: 重點回顧：ReLU 靠「正值段導數恒為 1」緩解梯度消失、靠「歸零負值」帶來稀疏；dying ReLU 由 Leaky / PReLU 修補；softmax 是唯一的跨層激活，輸出可當多類機率分布。
13de2fff1f10.en: Key takeaways: ReLU relieves vanishing gradients through "a derivative that is always 1 on the positive part" and brings sparsity by "zeroing out negative values"; dying ReLU is fixed by Leaky ReLU / PReLU; softmax is the only cross-layer activation, and its output can serve as a multi-class probability distribution.

69f5998f7f84.zh: 圖 11 13 種常見激活函數一覽（a 線性至 m Maxout）

35b8cc503f78.zh: 顯示 ReLU 家族四條曲線疊加（ReLU / ELU / Leaky / PReLU）
35b8cc503f78.en: Overlay the four ReLU-family curves (ReLU / ELU / Leaky / PReLU)

6e5a6d8b1c33.zh: 拖動 a 看 σ(a) 與 σ'(a) 變化；紅點標在曲線上、虛線框出值域。Softmax 用 3 元素向量、Maxout 取兩條線的最大。
6e5a6d8b1c33.en: Drag a to see how σ(a) and σ'(a) change; the red dot marks the point on the curve, and the dashed box outlines the range. Softmax uses a 3-element vector, and Maxout takes the maximum of two lines.

4203c33ef688.en: ReLU family colors: ReLU = blue, ELU = cyan, Leaky = green, PReLU = purple.

08a45d80264c.zh: 原理：激活函數注入非線性。點狀激活 $\sigma(a)$ 對每個輸入單獨作用；Softmax（式 33）在整層上做機率分配， Maxout（式 35）取多個線性單元的最大值。ReLU 家族共享「正半軸為 $a$」的骨架，差在負半軸：ReLU 全零、 ELU $\alpha(e^a-1)$、Leaky ReLU $0.01a$、PReLU $\alpha a$（$\alpha$ 可學）。可導性：ReLU/Leaky/PReLU 在 $a=0$ 不可導。
08a45d80264c.en: Principle: activation functions inject nonlinearity. An element-wise activation $\sigma(a)$ acts on each input separately; Softmax (Eq. 33) distributes probability over the whole layer, and Maxout (Eq. 35) takes the maximum of several linear units. The ReLU family shares the backbone "equals $a$ on the positive half-axis" and differs on the negative half-axis: ReLU is all zero, ELU is $\alpha(e^a-1)$, Leaky ReLU is $0.01a$, PReLU is $\alpha a$ ($\alpha$ is learnable). Differentiability: ReLU/Leaky/PReLU are not differentiable at $a=0$.

a2d35fbd3438.zh: 操作：下拉選 13 種激活之一，拖動 $a$（−5~5）看曲線上紅點、輸出 $\sigma(a)$ 與導數 $\sigma'(a)$ 的數值。 勾選「顯示 ReLU 家族四條曲線」切到疊加對比視圖。觀察什麼：線性導數恆 1、sigmoid 在 $a=0$ 得 $0.5$、 tanh 值域 $[-1,1]$、ReLU 在 $a=0$ 處導數「未定義」（左 0 右 1）、Softmax 輸出落在 $(0,1)$ 且整層和為 1。 正確基準：readout 的 $\sigma(a)$、$\sigma'(a)$ 與公式閉式完全一致；值域標記為定義域內實際 min/max。
a2d35fbd3438.en: How to use: pick one of the 13 activations from the drop-down, then drag $a$ (−5 to 5) to see the red dot on the curve and the values of the output $\sigma(a)$ and the derivative $\sigma'(a)$. Check "Overlay the four ReLU-family curves" to switch to the overlay comparison view. What to observe: the linear derivative is always 1, the sigmoid gives $0.5$ at $a=0$, tanh has range $[-1,1]$, ReLU's derivative at $a=0$ is "undefined" (0 on the left, 1 on the right), and Softmax's outputs fall in $(0,1)$ and sum to 1 over the whole layer. Correct baseline: the readout's $\sigma(a)$ and $\sigma'(a)$ match the closed-form formulas exactly; the range markers are the actual min/max over the domain.

c73089079779.zh: 為何 ReLU 被視為深度學習的里程碑？
c73089079779.en: Why is ReLU regarded as a milestone of deep learning?

7fd7d8e18e29.en: Its range is [-1,1] and it is zero-centered

9b5b4cf8149b.zh: 正值段導數恒為 1 避免梯度消失，並歸零負值帶來稀疏性
9b5b4cf8149b.en: Its derivative is always 1 on the positive part, avoiding vanishing gradients, and zeroing out negative values brings sparsity

44db2b83f16e.en: Its output can serve as a probability

276d09727f90.en: It has a nonzero slope on the negative interval

74d392415200.zh: 哪一種激活函數是「跨層」而非逐點作用，輸出可視為多類機率分布？
74d392415200.en: Which activation function acts "cross-layer" rather than element-wise, with an output that can be viewed as a multi-class probability distribution?

71968c7fbd9c.en: What does the "dying ReLU" problem refer to?

873420f74f5e.zh: ReLU 輸出太大導致爆炸
873420f74f5e.en: ReLU's output is too large, causing an explosion

050232687ad1.zh: 神經元在負區間導數為 0、權重不再更新而「死掉」
050232687ad1.en: A neuron's derivative is 0 on the negative interval, so its weights stop updating and it "dies"

2446302b21cd.zh: ReLU 無法處理正數輸入

2c4a20fd0ee7.en: ReLU is too slow to compute

7ef75fb914a4.zh: PReLU 與 Leaky ReLU 的主要差別是？
7ef75fb914a4.en: What is the main difference between PReLU and Leaky ReLU?

48b8a0cb86e9.zh: PReLU 的負區間斜率 \(\alpha\) 是可學習參數，Leaky 固定為 0.01
48b8a0cb86e9.en: PReLU's negative-interval slope \(\alpha\) is a learnable parameter, while Leaky ReLU fixes it at 0.01

8a97c97ce3df.en: PReLU can only be used in the output layer

b0dc14e51b49.en: Common loss functions: MSE / MAE / Huber / KL / Hinge / cross-entropy

8a5dcc6fee0f.zh: 損失函數（loss / cost function）決定網路「該往哪個方向調參數」。先統一符號：\(\theta\) 是網路權重、\(\boldsymbol{x}_i\) 是輸入、\(\mathbf{f}_o(\boldsymbol{x}_i)\) 是網路對該輸入的輸出、\(y_i\) 是目標標籤、\(b\) 是批次大小（一個 batch 的樣本數）、\(c\) 是類別數。下面按「回歸」和「分類」兩大類看六種。
8a5dcc6fee0f.en: The loss function (loss / cost function) decides “which way the network should adjust its parameters.” First, let us fix the notation: \(\theta\) is the network's weights, \(\boldsymbol{x}_i\) is the input, \(\mathbf{f}_o(\boldsymbol{x}_i)\) is the network's output for that input, \(y_i\) is the target label, \(b\) is the batch size (the number of samples in one batch), and \(c\) is the number of classes. Below we look at six of them, grouped into two families: “regression” and “classification.”

fb03d7bf2053.en: Common for regression: MSE, MAE, Huber

b0090b69d3b3.zh: MSE（均方誤差） (36)：minimize \(\sum_{i=1}^{b}(\mathbf{f}_o(\boldsymbol{x}_i)-y_i)^2\)。優點：平方之後到處可導，適合梯度下降。缺點：平方把離群值（outlier）放大，對離群值敏感。
b0090b69d3b3.en: MSE (mean squared error) (36): minimize \(\sum_{i=1}^{b}(\mathbf{f}_o(\boldsymbol{x}_i)-y_i)^2\). Pro: after squaring it is differentiable everywhere, which suits gradient descent. Con: squaring amplifies outliers, so it is sensitive to outliers.

bff602ccdce3.zh: MAE（平均絕對誤差） (37)：minimize \(\sum_{i=1}^{b}\lvert\mathbf{f}_o(\boldsymbol{x}_i)-y_i\rvert\)，又稱 Manhattan 距離。對離群值較穩健，且能鼓勵學到的表示變稀疏；缺點是在零點處不可導（實務上靠次梯度處理）。
bff602ccdce3.en: MAE (mean absolute error) (37): minimize \(\sum_{i=1}^{b}\lvert\mathbf{f}_o(\boldsymbol{x}_i)-y_i\rvert\), also known as the Manhattan distance. It is more robust to outliers and can encourage the learned representation to be sparse; the downside is that it is not differentiable at zero (in practice this is handled with subgradients).

918f5c28b430.zh: Huber (38)：折衷兩者。當 \(\lvert\mathbf{f}_o-y\rvert\le\delta\) 用 \(0.5(\mathbf{f}_o-y)^2\)（二次區，像 MSE）；否則用 \(\delta(\lvert\mathbf{f}_o-y\rvert-0.5\delta)\)（線性區，像 MAE）。\(\delta\gt 0\) 是可調的超參數，決定二次與線性區的切換門檻。
918f5c28b430.en: Huber (38): a compromise between the two. When \(\lvert\mathbf{f}_o-y\rvert\le\delta\) it uses \(0.5(\mathbf{f}_o-y)^2\) (the quadratic region, like MSE); otherwise it uses \(\delta(\lvert\mathbf{f}_o-y\rvert-0.5\delta)\) (the linear region, like MAE). \(\delta\gt 0\) is a tunable hyperparameter that sets the threshold for switching between the quadratic and linear regions.

82a5df928323.en: Common for classification: KL, Hinge, cross-entropy

3fbe61950ecd.zh: KL divergence (39)：minimize \(\sum_{i=1}^{b}\sum_{l=1}^{c}(y_i)_l\log\frac{(y_i)_l}{\mathbf{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_i)_l}\)。衡量預測分布 \(\mathbf{f}(\boldsymbol{x})\) 與目標分布 \(y\) 的「不相似度」。當 \(y\) 是 one-hot 時會退化成交叉熵；當 \(y\) 是軟標籤（soft target）時特別有用，例如知識蒸餾。
3fbe61950ecd.en: KL divergence (39): minimize \(\sum_{i=1}^{b}\sum_{l=1}^{c}(y_i)_l\log\frac{(y_i)_l}{\mathbf{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_i)_l}\). It measures the “dissimilarity” between the predicted distribution \(\mathbf{f}(\boldsymbol{x})\) and the target distribution \(y\). When \(y\) is one-hot it reduces to cross-entropy; it is especially useful when \(y\) is a soft label (soft target), for example in knowledge distillation.

6e3d6fb11384.zh: Hinge (40)：minimize \(\sum_{i=1}^{b}[m-y_i\mathbf{f}_o(\boldsymbol{x}_i)]_{+}\)，其中 \([\cdot]_{+}=\max(\cdot,0)\)（跟 ReLU 同型）、\(m\gt 0\) 是 margin 超參數、\(y_i\in\{-1,1\}\)。它不只懲罰分錯，也懲罰「分對了但離邊界太近」的樣本；當 \(\lvert\mathbf{f}_o\rvert\ge m\) 時損失為 0。也是 contrastive / triplet loss 的基礎。
6e3d6fb11384.en: Hinge (40): minimize \(\sum_{i=1}^{b}[m-y_i\mathbf{f}_o(\boldsymbol{x}_i)]_{+}\), where \([\cdot]_{+}=\max(\cdot,0)\) (the same form as ReLU), \(m\gt 0\) is the margin hyperparameter, and \(y_i\in\{-1,1\}\). It penalizes not only misclassified samples but also samples that are “classified correctly but too close to the boundary”; when \(\lvert\mathbf{f}_o\rvert\ge m\) the loss is 0. It is also the basis of contrastive / triplet loss.

51b3f00caa08.zh: Cross-Entropy（交叉熵） (41)：minimize \(-\sum_{i=1}^{b}\sum_{l=1}^{c}(\boldsymbol{y}_i)_l\log\mathbf{f}_o(\boldsymbol{x}_i)_l\)。分類最常用。前置條件：輸出層必須接 softmax（\(c\gt 2\) 類）或 sigmoid（二元），確保預測落在 [0,1] 且求和為 1。最小化它會讓網路把高機率分給正確類別，並在倒數第二層（penultimate layer）學出判別性特徵，有利下游檢索／聚類。
51b3f00caa08.en: Cross-entropy (41): minimize \(-\sum_{i=1}^{b}\sum_{l=1}^{c}(\boldsymbol{y}_i)_l\log\mathbf{f}_o(\boldsymbol{x}_i)_l\). It is the most common choice for classification. Prerequisite: the output layer must be followed by a softmax (for \(c\gt 2\) classes) or a sigmoid (binary), so that the predictions lie in [0,1] and sum to 1. Minimizing it makes the network assign high probability to the correct class and learn discriminative features in the penultimate layer, which helps downstream retrieval / clustering.

b027098417ce.zh: ADALINE 與 MADALINE：用連續誤差取代二元輸出
b027098417ce.en: ADALINE and MADALINE: replacing the binary output with a continuous error

74e4af4bfcba.zh: Perceptron 的兩個老毛病——依賴二元激活函數、泛化不佳——催生了另一個更穩定、解析上更好處理的學習法。1960 年 Bernard Widrow 與 Ted Hoff 提出了 ADALINE（Adaptive Linear Neuron，自適應線性神經元）。它的核心突破很簡單：用「加權和」當預測誤差的基準，而不是先用硬閾值切成 0/1 再比對。因為訓練時用的是連續數值輸出，權重更新更平滑，通常也帶來更好的泛化。
74e4af4bfcba.en: The perceptron's two old problems—its reliance on a binary activation function and poor generalization—gave rise to another learning method that is more stable and easier to handle analytically. In 1960, Bernard Widrow and Ted Hoff proposed ADALINE (Adaptive Linear Neuron). Its core breakthrough is simple: use the “weighted sum” as the basis for the prediction error, instead of first cutting it into 0/1 with a hard threshold and then comparing. Because training uses a continuous numeric output, the weight updates are smoother, which usually also brings better generalization.

78d88dd0bcc9.zh: ADALINE 怎麼算誤差：LMS 二次損失
78d88dd0bcc9.en: How ADALINE computes its error: the LMS quadratic loss

d8c83b30925e.zh: 回想 Perceptron 是把輸入加權、過閾值、輸出二元的 0/1 或 ±1。ADALINE 不這樣——它直接把真實標籤 \(y_i\) 跟「尚未套激活的加權和」\(\sum_j w_j x_{ij}+w_0\) 相比（Fig. 12）。訓練目標是最小化最小均方（LMS）誤差，這是一個二次損失，懲罰「預測與標籤」差值的平方：
d8c83b30925e.en: Recall that the perceptron weights the inputs, passes them through a threshold, and outputs a binary 0/1 or ±1. ADALINE does not do that—it directly compares the true label \(y_i\) with “the weighted sum before any activation is applied,” \(\sum_j w_j x_{ij}+w_0\) (Fig. 12). The training objective is to minimize the least mean squares (LMS) error, a quadratic loss that penalizes the square of the difference between “prediction and label”:

7ba5ba0751f7.zh: 這裡 \(b\) 是批次大小、\(y_i\) 是真實標籤、\(w_0\) 是偏置項。
7ba5ba0751f7.en: Here \(b\) is the batch size, \(y_i\) is the true label, and \(w_0\) is the bias term.

274b3f3c5253.zh: 這套學習法叫 LMS 演算法／Widrow-Hoff 法則，是對線性模型做梯度下降的早期形式。
274b3f3c5253.en: This learning method is called the LMS algorithm / Widrow-Hoff rule, and it is an early form of gradient descent on a linear model.

e91c4e786d77.zh: 為了應付更複雜的任務，Widrow 等人把多顆 ADALINE 單元堆疊成分層架構，稱為 MADALINE（Many ADALINEs，很多 ADALINE）（Fig. 13）。它的訓練規則一路演進：
e91c4e786d77.en: To handle more complex tasks, Widrow and colleagues stacked several ADALINE units into a layered architecture called MADALINE (Many ADALINEs) (Fig. 13). Its training rules evolved step by step:

e9c855d1e9b4.zh: 1962 年 MADALINE Rule I（MRI）：最早提出，但只能更新「輸入層到隱藏層」之間的權重。
e9c855d1e9b4.en: 1962, MADALINE Rule I (MRI): the first one proposed, but it could only update the weights “between the input layer and the hidden layer”.

ed9e18205c2e.zh: 1988 年 MADALINE Rule II（MRII）：突破限制，能同時更新輸入→隱藏與隱藏→輸出兩段連接。
ed9e18205c2e.en: 1988, MADALINE Rule II (MRII): broke through that limit and could update both the input→hidden and the hidden→output connections.

739d59ca48ea.zh: 1990 年 MADALINE Rule III（MRIII）：進一步改良，支援更深入的多層訓練。
739d59ca48ea.en: 1990, MADALINE Rule III (MRIII): improved further, supporting deeper multilayer training.

9681a6430da6.zh: 這些努力代表最早一批「建立並訓練深層神經架構」的嘗試，甚至發生在反向傳播被廣為採用之前。
9681a6430da6.en: These efforts represent some of the earliest attempts to “build and train deep neural architectures,” even before backpropagation was widely adopted.

0489fd205b46.zh: Logistic Regression：作為單神經元網路的機率分類器
0489fd205b46.en: Logistic Regression: A Probabilistic Classifier as a Single-Neuron Network

bad9349d2cac.zh: Logistic regression（邏輯回歸）並不屬於神經網路的歷史脈絡，但它長得極像「單神經元＋sigmoid 激活」的網路，而且能教我們「如何用機率解讀輸出、如何從最大似然推導損失」。我們把它放進來，是因為它在數學上把非線性激活與機率框架綁在一起——正是理解現代神經網路訓練的鑰匙。
bad9349d2cac.en: Logistic regression does not belong to the historical lineage of neural networks, but it looks remarkably like a "single neuron + sigmoid activation" network, and it can teach us "how to interpret the output as a probability and how to derive the loss from maximum likelihood." We include it because, mathematically, it ties a non-linear activation to a probabilistic framework, which is exactly the key to understanding how modern neural networks are trained.

31bda4b5404f.zh: 從 Bayes 公式出發，直接建模後驗
31bda4b5404f.en: Starting from Bayes' Formula: Model the Posterior Directly

6361e73a6998.zh: 設輸入 \(\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^d\)、二元標籤 \(y\in\{0,1\}\)。Bayes 公式給出：
6361e73a6998.en: Let the input be \(\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and the binary label \(y\in\{0,1\}\). Bayes' formula gives:

90e5ee180216.zh: \(\mathbb{P}(y\mid\boldsymbol{x})\) 叫後驗，\(\mathbb{P}(\boldsymbol{x}\mid y)\) 叫似然，\(\mathbb{P}(\boldsymbol{x}),\mathbb{P}(y)\) 叫先驗。
90e5ee180216.en: \(\mathbb{P}(y\mid\boldsymbol{x})\) is called the posterior, \(\mathbb{P}(\boldsymbol{x}\mid y)\) is called the likelihood, and \(\mathbb{P}(\boldsymbol{x}),\mathbb{P}(y)\) are called the priors.

18ac62f722ae.zh: 與 LDA 的關鍵差別：Linear Discriminant Analysis（線性判別分析）從似然與先驗下手去推後驗；Logistic regression 則直接建模後驗 \(\mathbb{P}(y\mid\boldsymbol{x})\)，跳過中間的生成模型。
18ac62f722ae.en: The key difference from LDA: linear discriminant analysis works from the likelihood and the prior to derive the posterior; logistic regression instead models the posterior \(\mathbb{P}(y\mid\boldsymbol{x})\) directly, skipping the generative model in between.

06596b848861.zh: 用 sigmoid 把線性回歸壓到 [0,1]
06596b848861.en: Using the Sigmoid to Squash Linear Regression into [0,1]

e7d262ff3e3d.zh: 歷史小記：logistic 函數 1845 年由 Verhulst 提出用來建模人口成長，1967 年 Walker & Duncan 加以推廣。邏輯回歸把分類當成「回歸出屬於某一類的機率」。做法是：先寫一個線性回歸 \(\boldsymbol{\beta}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}+\boldsymbol{\beta}_0\)。為了省去偏置項，它假設 \(\boldsymbol{x}=\left[1,x_1,\dots,x_d\right]^{\top}\)（多放一個 1 吸收 bias），於是線性部分變成 \(\boldsymbol{\beta}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\)，其中 \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\)。但線性回歸沒有上下界，不能當機率，所以用 logistic（sigmoid）函數把它壓到 [0,1]：
e7d262ff3e3d.en: A bit of history: the logistic function was proposed by Verhulst in 1845 to model population growth, and was generalized by Walker & Duncan in 1967. Logistic regression treats classification as "regressing the probability of belonging to a class." The approach: first write a linear regression \(\boldsymbol{\beta}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}+\boldsymbol{\beta}_0\). To get rid of the bias term, it assumes \(\boldsymbol{x}=\left[1,x_1,\dots,x_d\right]^{\top}\) (an extra 1 is added to absorb the bias), so the linear part becomes \(\boldsymbol{\beta}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\), where \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\). But linear regression has no upper or lower bound and cannot serve as a probability, so the logistic (sigmoid) function is used to squash it into [0,1]:

393f1776271a.zh: 如 Fig. 15 所示，logistic regression 可視為只有一顆神經元、激活函數是 sigmoid 的網路。
393f1776271a.en: As shown in Fig. 15, logistic regression can be viewed as a network with only one neuron whose activation function is the sigmoid.

3b505b66a7a8.en: Maximum Likelihood: From the Posterior to the Log-Posterior

d293301790d7.zh: 把東西寫成矩陣會更乾淨。定義 \(\boldsymbol{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{(d+1)\times n}\)（第一列全為 1）、\(\boldsymbol{W}=\operatorname{diag}(P(1-P))\)、\(\boldsymbol{y}\) 為標籤向量、\(\boldsymbol{p}\) 為目前預測的機率向量，則：

43691c5e62ba.zh: 這一節看兩個「概念重要、但不在深度學習主線」的模型：RBF 網路（監督，用固定基函數）與 Self-Organizing Map（無監督，自組織聚類）。它們分別展示了「用固定的核函數當特徵轉換」與「靠自組織在無標籤下揭露資料結構」這兩種不同的思路。

They illustrate two different ideas, respectively: "using a fixed kernel function as a feature transformation" and "revealing the structure of unlabeled data through self-organization."

a5c32fe18fd9.zh: RBF 網路：兩層結構，第一層固定基函數
a5c32fe18fd9.en: RBF Networks: A Two-Layer Structure with Fixed Basis Functions in the First Layer

dd66e4f753e6.zh: Radial Basis Function（徑向基函數）網路由 Broomhead & Lowe 於 1988 年提出。如 Fig. 16，它是兩層架構：
dd66e4f753e6.en: The Radial Basis Function network was proposed by Broomhead & Lowe in 1988. As shown in Fig. 16, it has a two-layer architecture:

295ba1d6b09a.zh: 第一層：把輸入 \(\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^d\) 接到 \(m\) 個固定的基函數 \(\phi_i(\boldsymbol{x}),\,i=1,\dots,m\)。常用的基函數如 Gaussian 或 logistic（sigmoid）：
295ba1d6b09a.en: First layer: connects the input \(\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^d\) to \(m\) fixed basis functions \(\phi_i(\boldsymbol{x}),\,i=1,\dots,m\). Commonly used basis functions include the Gaussian and the logistic (sigmoid):

3faaf746c9c8.zh: 其中 \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_i,\sigma_i^2\) 是均值與變異數。第一層不訓練：先對訓練資料跑 K-means 取 \(m\) 個群心當均值 \(\{\boldsymbol{\mu}_i\}\)，再由群的變異數決定 \(\{\sigma_i\}\)。
3faaf746c9c8.en: where \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_i,\sigma_i^2\) are the mean and variance. The first layer is not trained: first run K-means on the training data to obtain \(m\) cluster centroids as the means \(\{\boldsymbol{\mu}_i\}\), then determine \(\{\sigma_i\}\) from the variances of the clusters.

a61dc7607755.zh: 第二層：可訓練權重 \(\boldsymbol{W}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times k}\)，把基函數輸出映射到最終 \(k\) 個預測。
a61dc7607755.en: Second layer: trainable weights \(\boldsymbol{W}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times k}\) map the outputs of the basis functions to the final \(k\) predictions.

9f2d394c2497.zh: 輸出是基函數的加權平均（additive model）：\(\widehat{y}_j=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_{ij}\phi_i(\boldsymbol{x})\) (61)。
9f2d394c2497.en: The output is a weighted average of the basis functions (additive model): \(\widehat{y}_j=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_{ij}\phi_i(\boldsymbol{x})\) (61).

1968fb42d283.en: Solving for the Weights by Least Squares

c310449c3026.zh: 把 \(n\) 筆資料寫成矩陣，\(\widehat{\boldsymbol{Y}}=\boldsymbol{W}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\Phi}\) (62)，其中 \(\boldsymbol{\Phi}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) 每行是某筆資料對所有基函數的值。最小化 Frobenius 範數損失：
c310449c3026.en: Writing the \(n\) data points as matrices, \(\widehat{\boldsymbol{Y}}=\boldsymbol{W}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\Phi}\) (62), where each column of \(\boldsymbol{\Phi}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) holds the values of all basis functions for one data point. Minimize the Frobenius norm loss:

a3cde06849c7.zh: 展開並用 tr 的線性與循環性質，對 \(\boldsymbol{W}\) 求導置零得 \(\boldsymbol{\Phi}\boldsymbol{\Phi}^{\top}\boldsymbol{W}=\boldsymbol{\Phi}\boldsymbol{Y}^{\top}\)
a3cde06849c7.en: Expanding it and using the linearity and cyclic property of tr, then setting the derivative with respect to \(\boldsymbol{W}\) to zero, gives \(\boldsymbol{\Phi}\boldsymbol{\Phi}^{\top}\boldsymbol{W}=\boldsymbol{\Phi}\boldsymbol{Y}^{\top}\)

bd082e5f1042.en: \(\boldsymbol{W}=(\boldsymbol{\Phi}\boldsymbol{\Phi}^{\top})^{-1}\boldsymbol{\Phi}\boldsymbol{Y}^{\top}\) (64); if \(\boldsymbol{\Phi}\boldsymbol{\Phi}^{\top}\) is singular, use the pseudo-inverse instead: \(\boldsymbol{W}=(\boldsymbol{\Phi}\boldsymbol{\Phi}^{\top})^{\dagger}\boldsymbol{\Phi}\boldsymbol{Y}^{\top}\) (65)

87f83a5c9cfe.zh: SOM（Kohonen 網路）：無監督單層聚類

6742b05623b1.zh: Self-Organizing Map 由 Kohonen（1982）提出，用於無監督學習與聚類，不做監督預測。它是單層網路：把輸入 \(\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^d\) 接到 \(k\) 顆神經元，每顆代表一個簇原型。神經元按預設的 1D 或 2D 拓撲排列（Fig. 17），讓相似的輸入激發相鄰的神經元。每顆神經元 \(j\) 在其拓撲上有鄰域 \(\mathcal{N}_j^{(\tau)}\)，訓練過程中會逐漸縮小。
6742b05623b1.en: The Self-Organizing Map was proposed by Kohonen (1982) and is used for unsupervised learning and clustering, not for supervised prediction. It is a single-layer network: it connects the input \(\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^d\) to \(k\) neurons, each representing a cluster prototype. The neurons are arranged in a predefined 1D or 2D topology (Fig. 17), so that similar inputs excite neighboring neurons. Each neuron \(j\) has a neighborhood \(\mathcal{N}_j^{(\tau)}\) in this topology, which gradually shrinks during training.

a4e34c5209d4.en: The training algorithm has five steps:

0a5473de0ee7.zh: 初始化：權重設為小隨機值；所有鄰域 \(\mathcal{N}_j^{(0)}\) 設為神經元格子的一半；學習率 \(\eta^{(0)}\in(0,1]\)。
0a5473de0ee7.en: Initialization: set the weights to small random values; set every neighborhood \(\mathcal{N}_j^{(0)}\) to half of the neuron grid; learning rate \(\eta^{(0)}\in(0,1]\).

81393e5a4f06.zh: 選輸入與勝者：挑一筆 \(\boldsymbol{x}\)，取勝者 \(z:=\arg\min_j\sum_{i=1}^{d}\lVert x_i-w_{ij}\rVert_2\) (67)
81393e5a4f06.en: Pick an input and the winner: pick a sample \(\boldsymbol{x}\) and take the winner \(z:=\arg\min_j\sum_{i=1}^{d}\lVert x_i-w_{ij}\rVert_2\) (67)

53557384f101.zh: 鄰域更新：只更新勝者鄰域內的神經元權重 \(w_{ij}^{(\tau+1)}:=w_{ij}^{(\tau)}+\eta^{(\tau)}(x_i-w_{ij}^{(\tau)})\) 若 \(j\in\mathcal{N}_z^{(\tau)}\)，否則不變 (68)
53557384f101.en: Neighborhood update: update only the weights of neurons in the winner's neighborhood, \(w_{ij}^{(\tau+1)}:=w_{ij}^{(\tau)}+\eta^{(\tau)}(x_i-w_{ij}^{(\tau)})\) if \(j\in\mathcal{N}_z^{(\tau)}\), and leave them unchanged otherwise (68)

a98aad37c93b.zh: 衰減：降低學習率 \(\eta^{(\tau+1)}:=\eta^{(0)}(1-\tau/t)\) (69)，且鄰域對半縮 \(\mathcal{N}_j^{(\tau+1)}:=\mathcal{N}_j^{(\tau)}/2\) (70)
a98aad37c93b.en: Decay: lower the learning rate \(\eta^{(\tau+1)}:=\eta^{(0)}(1-\tau/t)\) (69), and halve the neighborhood \(\mathcal{N}_j^{(\tau+1)}:=\mathcal{N}_j^{(\tau)}/2\) (70)

3183ee756cb6.zh: 迭代：\(\tau\) 加一，回到第 2 步。
3183ee756cb6.en: Iterate: increment \(\tau\) by one and go back to step 2.

0d803db37f20.zh: 測試階段，把 \(\boldsymbol{x}\) 送入，由式 (67) 求得的勝者神經元就決定它所屬的簇。
0d803db37f20.en: In the test phase, feed in \(\boldsymbol{x}\); the winning neuron found by Eq. (67) determines which cluster it belongs to.
